```{r,echo=FALSE}
pn = function(coeffs,pows){
    pows = pows[coeffs!=0]
    coeffs = coeffs[coeffs!=0]
    ex1 = paste0("{",coeffs,"}x^{",pows,"}",collapse="+")
    ex1 = gsub("+{-","-{",ex1,fixed=T)
    ex1 = gsub("{1}x^{0}","1",ex1,fixed=T)
    ex1 = gsub("{-1}x^{0}","-1",ex1,fixed=T)
    ex1 = gsub("{1}x","x",ex1,fixed=T)
    ex1 = gsub("{-1}x","-x",ex1,fixed=T)
    ex1 = gsub("x^{0}","",ex1,fixed=T)
    ex1 = gsub("x^{1}","x",ex1,fixed=T)
    ex1 = gsub("+-","-",ex1,fixed=T)
    if(ex1 == ""){
        ex1 = "0"
    }
    return(ex1)
}
# b^2-4*a*c
library(numbers)


while(T){
    ac1 = sample(3:6,1)
    b = ac1*2*sample(c(-1,1),1)
    
    ac2 = primeFactors(ac1^2)
    npf = length(ac2)
    npfa = sample(0:npf,1)
    if(npfa==0){
        a = 1
    } else {
        a = prod(sample(ac2,npfa))
    }
    c = round(ac1^2/a)
    
    qt = sample(-1:1,1)
    wc = sample(1:2,1)
    
    if(wc == 1){
        a = a-qt
    } else {
        c = c-qt
    }
    
    D = b^2-4*a*c
    if(min(c(a,b,c))>0 && max(abs(c(a,b,c)))<13){break}
}

if(D<0){
    s1 = "D<0"
    s2 = "two complex solutions."
    sol = "001"
}
if(D==0){
    s1 = "D=0"
    s2 = "one real solution."
    sol = "010"
}
if(D>0){
    s1 = "D>0"
    s2 = "two real solutions."
    sol = "100"
}

```


Question
========

Consider the quadratic equation:

$$`r pn(c(a,b,c),2:0)`=0$$

Does the equation have two real solutions, one real solution, or two complex solutions?

*Hint: Calculate the [discriminant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadratic_equation#Discriminant).*

Answerlist
--------

* Two real solutions
* One real solution
* Two complex solutions


Solution
========

The discriminant, $D$, is the expression under the radical in the quadratic formula.

$$D=b^2-4ac$$

| If | Then |
|:---:|:---:|
| $D<0$ | There are two complex solutions |
| $D=0$ | There is one real solution |
| $D>0$ | There are two real solutions |

Calculate the discriminant.


$$D=(`r b`)^2-4(`r a`)(`r c`)$$


$$D=`r b^2`-`r 4*a*c`$$


$$D=`r D`$$

Because $`r s1`$ we know the equation has `r s2`
